principles: Per-story declaration only — generated artifacts must be tied to the story that produced them, not a global allowlist
Reference required — every declared artifact must link to an intentRef or delivery promiseId so DONE can prove user-visible coverage
Reuse B-6326 classifier injection — do NOT carve a new code path for declared artifacts; populate declaredArtifactPaths from the per-story declaration
drivers: B-c9f5 field report: tests/output/bl21_lacz_ecoli_minicell/prodenovo_viewer.json was a real product output but classifier had no declaration channel
B-6326 left declaredArtifactPaths empty — B-cf60 is the wiring story
B-4b22 (Material Dirty Gate Policy, next) needs a populated declared_artifact_changes category to differentiate from unexpected_dirty_files in policy decisions

options.name: A: Per-story declared-artifacts.json + classifier injection + DONE gate reference check
pros: Story-scoped declaration ties artifacts to user-visible work
Reuses existing classifier injection (declaredArtifactPaths) — minimal new code surface
DONE gate proves artifact was referenced before passing — no silent generated-output loosening
cons: Adds one CLI handler (artifact_declare) + one store.write* method + classifier wiring through config — 3 small touch points
DONE gate gains one more blocker type — risk of false positives if reference matching is wrong

options.name: B: Extend checklist item schema with declaredArtifacts: string[] field
pros: No new file or store.write* method
Declaration co-located with the checklist item that promises the artifact
cons: Mutates the established checklist schema mid-flight; backward compat headache
Hard to declare artifacts that span multiple items
Cannot record reason / why this artifact is expected

options.name: C: Global koala.config.json allowlist for declared paths
pros: Single config edit, no story-level CLI
cons: Violates per-story principle — orphans declared paths from any story
No DONE gate hook — generated files silently pass forever
Re-creates the B-c9f5 problem in a different shape

chosen: A: Per-story declared-artifacts.json + classifier injection + DONE gate reference check
rationale: Choose A because it satisfies the principle of per-story scoping AND reuses B-6326 classifier injection (single source of truth for category routing). The new declared-artifacts.json file fits the existing store.ts write* pattern, gets auto-committed by B-3506, and the DONE gate reference check enforces the safety boundary the story description requires. Reject B because mutating the checklist schema mid-flight is risky and forces artifacts to attach to a single item even when they span multiple. Reject C because it directly contradicts the user-stated 'narrow story-local schema instead of global ignore rules' constraint from B-cf60 CHK-001 context.

preMortem.scenario: Declared artifact path becomes a backdoor: a future operator declares tests/output/* (wildcard) and silently passes unexpected outputs
preMortem.consequence: Generated files silently merged without verification; B-c9f5 incident shape returns
preMortem.mitigation: Handler accepts only exact relative paths (no glob, no *, no .., no leading /). Runtime check at handler entry. Smoke test: artifact_declare with path containing * or ** throws.

preMortem.scenario: DONE gate reference check matches loosely — declared artifact tied to a non-existent intentRef silently passes
preMortem.trigger: Reference check only verifies the field is non-empty without confirming intentRef actually exists in checklist
preMortem.consequence: User declares artifact with bogus intentRef like X-001:happy:0; DONE passes; no verification actually covers the artifact
preMortem.mitigation: Reference check at DONE gate must validate intentRef matches an existing checklist.items[*].verificationIntent[lane][index] OR a delivery-check.docsPromises[*].promiseId. Mismatch → [unreferenced_declared_artifact] blocker. Smoke test: declared artifact with bogus intentRef → DONE blocked.

preMortem.scenario: Materially regressed code in tests/output/foo.json passes because path is declared
preMortem.trigger: Declared path is also used by smoke tests; classification labels it declared_artifact_changes; gate trusts the label
preMortem.consequence: Real material regression in tests/output/foo.json (e.g., snapshot drift bug) silently merged
preMortem.mitigation: Declaration is presentation-only — does NOT remove the path from material checks. Re-verify: smoke test passes when declared path is changed in a way that matches expected output, FAILS when path changes in unexpected way (this requires the underlying verification command to still run). B-cf60 only adds a label channel; it does not change blocking semantics. B-4b22 is the policy story — until then, declared_artifact_changes remains blocking just like unexpected. Smoke explicitly asserts declared_artifact_changes is NOT auto-passed by B-cf60.
